**Karen S. Lynch** ([née](Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name") Rohan, born December 30, 1963) is an American businesswoman and the president and [chief executive officer](Chief_executive_officer "Chief executive officer") of [CVS Health](CVS_Health "CVS Health"). Lynch serves on the board of directors of [AHIP](America's_Health_Insurance_Plans "America's Health Insurance Plans"), CVS Health, and [U.S. Bancorp](U.S._Bancorp "U.S. Bancorp"). In 2015, she became the first female president of <Aetna>. She has held executive positions at [Magellan Health Services](Magellan_Health "Magellan Health") and <Cigna>. In 2021, she became the highest-ranking female chief executive on the [Fortune 500](Fortune_500 "Fortune 500") list.[[1]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-powerful-1)

## Early life and education

Lynch was born on December 30, 1963, in [Ware, Massachusetts](Ware%2C_Massachusetts "Ware, Massachusetts").[[2]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-2) She attended Ware Junior/Senior High School and graduated in 1980.[[3]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-3) Lynch attended [Carroll School of Management](Carroll_School_of_Management "Carroll School of Management") at [Boston College](Boston_College "Boston College"), where she received a bachelor’s degree in Accounting and has a Certified Public Accountant (CPA) certification.[[4]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-distilnfo-4) Upon graduating, she started her financial career in the Boston office of [Ernst & Young](Ernst_%26_Young "Ernst & Young"), where she specialized in insurance.[[5]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-intro-5)[[4]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-distilnfo-4)

## Career

Lynch credits her chosen career path in health care to her family life experiences.[[5]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-intro-5) She spent nearly a decade in insurance before returning to graduate school to pursue her MBA, saying, "I wanted to broaden my financial background to have more exposure to the business aspects of running a company".[[4]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-distilnfo-4) In 2004, Lynch was appointed president of Cigna Dental.[[6]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-6) The following year, she was named to a newly-created position that combines leadership of Cigna Group Insurance and Cigna Dental.[[7]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-7) She left Cigna in 2009 to become president of Magellan Health Services.[[8]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-CEO-8)[[9]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-9)

Lynch stayed with Magellan until 2012, when she joined Aetna as executive vice president and head of Specialty Products.[[10]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-10) Three months after joining Aetna, Lynch led the integration of [Coventry Health Care](Coventry_Health_Care "Coventry Health Care"), which was the largest health care acquisition at the time.[[11]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-leadersmag-11) In 2015, Lynch became Aetna's first female president, a role she retained through the $70 billion acquisition of Aetna by CVS Health in 2018.[[12]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-12)[[13]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-13)

During the [COVID-19 pandemic](COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), Lynch took the helm as president and chief executive officer of CVS Health on February 1, 2021, following the retirement of Larry Merlo. The appointment made her the highest-ranking female CEO on the Fortune 500 list and the 40th female chief executive on the Fortune 500 list.[[14]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-Valinsky-14)[[15]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-Forbes-15) Under Lynch's leadership, CVS Health administered the [COVID-19 vaccine](COVID-19_vaccine "COVID-19 vaccine") in more than 40,000 long-term care facilities and in [CVS Pharmacy](CVS_Pharmacy "CVS Pharmacy") locations in 50 states, Puerto Rico and Washington, D.C.[[16]](Karen_S._Lynch#cite_note-16)

Brewer** (born 1962) is an American businesswoman, and was the CEO of [Walgreens Boots Alliance](Walgreens_Boots_Alliance "Walgreens Boots Alliance"), before stepping down in September 2023.[[1]](Rosalind_Brewer#cite_note-1) Brewer is the first woman to become CEO of [Walgreens Boots Alliance](Walgreens_Boots_Alliance "Walgreens Boots Alliance"), group president and COO of <Starbucks>, and CEO of [Sam's Club](Sam's_Club "Sam's Club").[[2]](Rosalind_Brewer#cite_note-usat-2)

## Early life and education

Rosalind Brewer was born in 1962 in <Detroit>, <Michigan>,[[4]](Rosalind_Brewer#cite_note-:1-4) the youngest of five children; they were the first generation in her family to attend college.[[4]](Rosalind_Brewer#cite_note-:1-4) Due to her inclination for math and science, Brewer was interested in pursuing a career as a [physician](Physician "Physician").[[5]](Rosalind_Brewer#cite_note-:2-5)

In 1980, upon graduating from [Cass Technical High School](Cass_Technical_High_School "Cass Technical High School") in Detroit, Brewer enrolled at [Spelman College](Spelman_College "Spelman College") in <Atlanta>, [Georgia](Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)") where she completed her bachelor's degree in chemistry.[[6]](Rosalind_Brewer#cite_note-profile-6)[[7]](Rosalind_Brewer#cite_note-walmart-7) She decided not to pursue a career in medicine, and began working at <Kimberly-Clark> as a research technician.

In 2020, she was ranked tenth on the *<Forbes>* list of "[The World's 100 Most Powerful Women](Forbes_list_of_The_World's_100_Most_Powerful_Women "Forbes list of The World's 100 Most Powerful Women")".[[3]](Gail_Koziara_Boudreaux#cite_note-Forbes_Powerful_Women_2020-3) From 2008 to 2014, she was on the *[Fortune](Fortune_(magazine) "Fortune (magazine)")* list of powerful women, peaking at No. 25.[[4]](Gail_Koziara_Boudreaux#cite_note-4) In 2015, she formed her own healthcare consulting company, GKB Global Health, LLC. In 2017, she became CEO of [Elevance Health](Elevance_Health "Elevance Health"), now the second-largest American company with a woman CEO.

## High school

Boudreaux attended Chicopee Comprehensive High School in [Chicopee, Massachusetts](Chicopee%2C_Massachusetts "Chicopee, Massachusetts"). Her team twice won the state championship. At 17, she averaged 23.4 points and 20 rebounds a game for the Chicopee Comprehensive girls' basketball team. She ultimately scored a school-record 1,719 career points and was named a Parade All American her senior year. The 6'2" senior center also held the Massachusetts girls' state shot-put record with a throw of 44 feet, six inches.[[5]](Gail_Koziara_Boudreaux#cite_note-SI1978-5)

## College

Koziara led the Big Green women's basketball in scoring for three consecutive years, and still holds a substantial number of school records. She became Dartmouth's all-time leading scorer and rebounder, with 1,933 points and 1,635 rebounds in 89 games.[[6]](Gail_Koziara_Boudreaux#cite_note-:0-6) She also was named [Ivy League](Ivy_League "Ivy League") Player of the Year three straight seasons, and became a two-time [Academic All-American](Academic_All-American "Academic All-American") and third team <All-American> as well. Koziara was honored by the NCAA as a Silver Anniversary Award winner and inducted into the New England Basketball Hall of Fame and Dartmouth's Wearers of the Green Hall of Fame. She led the Big Green to the first of their many Ivy League championships.[[6]](Gail_Koziara_Boudreaux#cite_note-:0-6) She also won four straight Ivy League women's shot put titles, with a throw of 46 feet, four inches her senior year. That same year she earned All American recognition in the shot put.[[7]](Gail_Koziara_Boudreaux#cite_note-SI1982-7)

She graduated cum laude from [Dartmouth College](Dartmouth_College "Dartmouth College") in 1982.[[8]](Gail_Koziara_Boudreaux#cite_note-:1-8)[[9]](Gail_Koziara_Boudreaux#cite_note-9) She attended business school at [Columbia University](Columbia_University "Columbia University") and graduated with high honors in 1989.[[6]](Gail_Koziara_Boudreaux#cite_note-:0-6)[[8]](Gail_Koziara_Boudreaux#cite_note-:1-8)

## Professional career

She spent 20 years at AETNA, then in 2002 was named president of Blue Cross/Blue Shield of Illinois. She became the executive vice president for External Operations at [Health Care Service Corporation](Health_Care_Service_Corporation "Health Care Service Corporation"), which encompasses Blue Cross/Blue Shield of Illinois.

In May 2008 she became executive [vice president](Vice_president "Vice president") of UnitedHealthcare at [UnitedHealth Group](UnitedHealth_Group "UnitedHealth Group"). From January 2011 to November 2014, she served as the [chief executive officer](Chief_executive_officer "Chief executive officer") of UnitedHealthcare,[[10]](Gail_Koziara_Boudreaux#cite_note-10) the biggest US insurer, serving 45 million customers with revenue of $120 billion.[[11]](Gail_Koziara_Boudreaux#cite_note-11)

**Mary Teresa Barra** (née **Makela**; born December 24, 1961) is an American businesswoman who has been the chair[[1]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-1) and [chief executive officer](Chief_executive_officer "Chief executive officer") (CEO) of [General Motors](General_Motors "General Motors") since January 15, 2014.[[2]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-2) She is the first female CEO of a ['Big Three' automaker](Big_Three_(automobile_manufacturers) "Big Three (automobile manufacturers)").[[3]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-nyt-3)[[4]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-General_Motors-4)[[5]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-5) In December 2013, GM named her to succeed [Daniel Akerson](Daniel_Akerson "Daniel Akerson") as CEO.[[3]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-nyt-3) Prior to being named CEO, Barra was executive vice president of global product development, purchasing, and supply chain.[[3]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-nyt-3)[[4]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-General_Motors-4)

## Early life

Barra was born in [Royal Oak, Michigan](Royal_Oak%2C_Michigan "Royal Oak, Michigan"), to parents of [Finnish](Finnish_American "Finnish American") descent.[[6]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-CNNFortune-6)[[7]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-HelsinginSanomat-7) Her grandfather, Viktor Mäkelä, moved to the US and married Maria Luoma, a Finnish immigrant from <Teuva>. They lived in [Mountain Iron, Minnesota](Mountain_Iron%2C_Minnesota "Mountain Iron, Minnesota") and had three children, including a son named Reino,[[8]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-8) called Ray. Barra's father, Ray, married a second-generation Finnish American named Eva Pyykkönen, and Mary was born in 1961.

## Education

Barra graduated from the General Motors Institute (now [Kettering University](Kettering_University "Kettering University")) in 1985, where she obtained a [Bachelor of Science](Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") in [Electrical Engineering](Electrical_Engineering "Electrical Engineering").[[9]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-9) Barra was inducted into the engineering honor society [Tau Beta Pi](Tau_Beta_Pi#Undergraduate_eligibility_requirements "Tau Beta Pi")[[10]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-taubetapi2018-10) (MI Zeta class of 1985) and the honor society [IEEE-Eta Kappa Nu](Eta_Kappa_Nu "Eta Kappa Nu") (Theta Epsilon chapter 1983) while at Kettering University. She then attended [Stanford Graduate School of Business](Stanford_Graduate_School_of_Business "Stanford Graduate School of Business") on a GM fellowship, receiving a [Master of Business Administration](Master_of_Business_Administration "Master of Business Administration") degree in 1990.[[11]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-bb-11)

## Career

### General Motors

Barra started working for General Motors in 1980 as a [co-op student](Cooperative_education "Cooperative education") when she was 18 years old.[[12]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-shm-12) Her job was checking fender panels and inspecting hoods, and she used this job to pay for her college tuition.[[13]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-13) She subsequently held a variety of engineering and administrative positions, including managing the [Detroit/Hamtramck Assembly](Detroit/Hamtramck_Assembly "Detroit/Hamtramck Assembly") plant.[[11]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-bb-11)

In February 2008, she became vice president of Global Manufacturing Engineering. In July 2009, she advanced to the position of vice president of Global Human Resources, which she held until February 2011 when she was named executive vice president of Global Product Development.[[11]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-bb-11)[[14]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-14) The latter position included responsibilities for design; she worked to reduce the number of [automobile platforms](Automobile_platforms "Automobile platforms") in [GM](List_of_GM_platforms "List of GM platforms").[[3]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-nyt-3) In August 2013, her vice president responsibility was extended to include Global Purchasing and Supply Chain.[[15]](Mary_Barra#cite_note-gm-15)
